evidence: app/src/index.tsx:78-82 — abilities route plus import at :6 must be deleted by hand
app/src/views/details.tsx:55-78 — loadAbility/AbilityPage live in a file shared with moves and types, so removal is surgery, not file deletion
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:286-296 — the Pokémon page's Abilities section links to /abilities and must be edited too
app/src/views/layout.tsx:27-36 — nav has no abilities link, so nothing to unlink and no dead code left behind
removability.rationale: Removing a feature means three scattered, careful edits rather than deleting a directory plus a nav link; the details.tsx multi-feature file is the main obstacle.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:28 — spriteUrl is the single sprite-URL builder; used only by CardList (components.tsx:37), so the Deoxys-class sprite fix covers every list from one place
app/src/views/components.tsx:30-52 — CardList is the sole card renderer for home, move, ability, type and team lists
app/src/index.tsx:51 — SORT_KEYS duplicates the column list in pokemon.tsx:32-39; adding a moves column means updating both
app/src/views/home.tsx:43-46, app/src/views/team.tsx:51-62, app/src/data.ts:91-108 — Card objects are assembled in three independent places
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:78,224-230,288 — API payload handling is untyped (any), so a data-shape fix relies on runtime probing rather than the typechecker
changeability.rationale: Most fixes (sprite, humanize, sort order, move tables) land in one obvious, findable place; a few cross-file duplications (sort keys, card assembly, untyped payloads) keep it from being a 5.

evidence: app/src/api.ts — transport and caching are fully isolated behind api/apiUrl/apiList; views never touch fetch
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:4 — Pokémon view imports TeamButton/TEAM_SIZE from views/team.tsx, a cross-feature view dependency (the button belongs in shared components.tsx)
app/src/index.tsx:92-104 — /team/remove branches on a ?from=team magic query flag to choose the response fragment
app/src/views/team.tsx:94-115 — htmx wiring (hx-target closest .team-action) is colocated with the fragment the route returns; the server/client seam is the endpoint contract, clear if implicit
coupling.rationale: Layering is genuinely clean (routes → loaders → shared data helpers), with two mild tangles: a view importing another view and a query-flag branch in a route.

evidence: app/src/data.ts:84-91 — Card with optional types and note models the real variation across the five card lists without flag parameters
app/src/views/components.tsx:35 — CardList's action render-prop absorbs the team page's remove button instead of a boolean flag
app/src/views/pokemon.tsx:141-204 — MoveTable is reused for both initial render and htmx sort swaps, one component serving two routes
app/src/views/details.tsx:6-42 vs 55-78 vs 96-140 — Move/Ability/Type pages each hand-roll the same h1 + dl + Sections skeleton; an Items page would copy ~40 lines of loader+page boilerplate
app/src/views/components.tsx:17-26 — TypeBadge's link boolean is the only flag creep, and it's harmless
abstraction_design.rationale: Abstractions sit where the app's real variation is (cards, sections, partial-swap tables) and stretch without flags; the detail-page skeleton is copied rather than shared, which caps it at 4.

findings.issue: API payloads flow through the whole app as `any` (16+ casts: pokemon, moves, abilities, type records, generations), so refactorings of data mapping get no compile-time help and the typecheck script can't catch mistakes.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal response interfaces (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type) in a shared types module and have api<T>/loaders return them; drop the per-line casts.

findings.issue: The Pokémon view imports TeamButton and TEAM_SIZE from views/team.tsx, coupling two feature views; removing or reshaping the team feature forces edits to the Pokémon page.
findings.suggestion: Move TeamButton and TEAM_SIZE into views/components.tsx (or a small team/team-button module) so feature views depend only on shared primitives.

findings.issue: details.tsx bundles three unrelated resources (moves, abilities, types), so feature removal means excising functions from a shared file and an Items section means appending to an ever-growing one.
findings.suggestion: Split into views/moves.tsx, views/abilities.tsx, views/types.tsx, one resource per file, matching the existing home/pokemon/team convention.

findings.issue: Card assembly ({...species, types: typesById.get(id) ?? []}) is duplicated in three loaders (home.tsx:43-46, team.tsx:51-62, data.ts:91-108 via cardsForPokemon); a change to card shape touches all three.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single toCards(species, typesById) helper in data.ts and have all three loaders use it.

findings.issue: The set of sortable move columns is defined twice: SORT_KEYS in the route and COLUMNS/SortKey in pokemon.tsx:32-39; adding a column silently desyncs validation from rendering.
findings.suggestion: Export COLUMNS (or just the key list) from pokemon.tsx and build SORT_KEYS from it.

findings.issue: /team/remove branches on a magic ?from=team query flag to decide which fragment to return — a flag-parameter smell embedded in the URL.
findings.suggestion: Either a dedicated endpoint (e.g. POST /team/remove/:name returning the team content) or decide from an explicit HX-Target header rather than a hand-rolled query param.

findings.issue: typesByPokemonId rebuilds a full species→types map by scanning every type record on every call, recomputed separately by home.tsx:30 and team.tsx:56; only the raw responses are cached, not the derived map.
findings.suggestion: Memoize the derived map (module-level promise) or compute it once and pass it down, so type-derivation changes land in one call site.

findings.issue: All 12 routes live inline in one index.tsx rather than grouped per feature with app.route(), so every added/removed resource edits the same file against the Hono best practice of organizing by feature.
findings.suggestion: At this scale it's tolerable; if more resources (items, berries) arrive, split into Hono sub-apps per feature and mount them.

summary: This is a well-layered htmx/Hono app: transport/caching, derived data, and per-feature views each have exactly one home, and the shared components (Card, CardList, Section, MoveTable) absorb the app's real variation without flag creep. The recurring costs to future editors are untyped API payloads, a multi-feature details.tsx that forces surgery for removals and copy-paste for new resources, and small duplications (sort keys, card assembly). Most change scenarios land in one or two obvious places; only feature removal is genuinely scattered.
